correctness.rationale: The crown distance table gives an exact local criterion at every vertex. A complete occupancy argument proves that all sets of cardinality at least \(4\) satisfy it, no set of cardinality at most \(2\) does, and the valid triples are exactly the stated one-sided or unmatched-support triples. Counting those triples gives the coefficient of \(x^3\); all higher coefficients are binomial. The standalone checker reconstructs distances and verifies every subset for \(3\le n\le9\).

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical matching-deleted biclique and disjunctive total domination is a natural redundancy relaxation of total domination. The result gives a complete all-set classification with a sharp saturation threshold at cardinality \(4\), an exact boundary description at cardinality \(3\), the full polynomial, and the exact minimum-set multiplicity. This is a structural finite-family theorem rather than a routine recomputation of a known scalar invariant.
